subject.title: Pause blocked background Claude CLI auth probes

question: Should a generic five-second `claude auth status --json` timeout disable background Auto CLI probing for six hours, or should long suppression require stronger evidence of a blocked Keychain prompt?
rationale: Timeouts are not specific to Keychain dialogs, and this choice changes the Claude Auto fallback availability contract for existing users.

options.title: Narrow long cooldown
options.body: Use a short timeout backoff and apply a multi-hour cooldown only when the blocked-prompt condition can be identified reliably.

options.title: Accept six-hour suppression
options.body: Keep the current fail-closed behavior and explicitly accept that any transient timeout can remove background CLI usage for six hours.

options.title: Pause for runtime evidence
options.body: Hold the PR until packaged-app evidence distinguishes blocked Keychain prompts from ordinary slow or wrapped Claude CLI timeouts.

recommendation.title: Narrow long cooldown
recommendation.body: Use a short timeout backoff and apply a multi-hour cooldown only when the blocked-prompt condition can be identified reliably.

likelyOwner.reason: The repository owner merged the current authentication-status preflight and is best positioned to define its upgrade-compatibility contract.
